dialogues.speaker: Bhai
dialogues.text: Are all Mondstadters so sentimental?

dialogues.speaker: Bhai
dialogues.text: If you ask me, it's better to focus on what's going on around you. That's how you should live!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mondstadter?

dialogues.speaker: Bhai
dialogues.text: The old man over there, who is constantly murmuring, "May the Anemo Archon bless us."

dialogues.speaker: Bhai
dialogues.text: I don't have anything against the Anemo Archon but I think the old man is trapped in the wind, he's going nowhere.

dialogues.speaker: Bhai
dialogues.text: His wife was a smart and capable captain of a merchant fleet, and I was her chief mate.

dialogues.speaker: Bhai
dialogues.text: *sigh* If she saw that old guy behaving like this, she'd rise from the ground and slap him right on the head!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you.

dialogues.speaker: Bhai
dialogues.text: Never let any beautiful moments go amiss!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You don't like him?

dialogues.speaker: Bhai
dialogues.text: Honestly, I don't hate him at all. When he was young, he was passionate and talkative. He knew a great deal about poetry and singing, which was quite enviable.

dialogues.speaker: Bhai
dialogues.text: But now, his attitude is really driving me nuts. He could've done so much better than this!

dialogues.speaker: Bhai
dialogues.text: While you're alive, you should cherish what you have and live in the present instead of trapping yourself in the past.

dialogues.speaker: Bhai
dialogues.text: Old memories should be the nutrient of new life, not shackles keeping you in the endless loop of pain.

dialogues.speaker: Bhai
dialogues.text: The Greater Lord is a perfect example of this. She might have passed away, but what she left behind will nourish Sumeru for generations.

dialogues.speaker: Bhai
dialogues.text: This old thing has lived in Sumeru for so long yet still doesn't understand this. He hasn't learned a thing from her!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So you don't like him?

dialogues.speaker: Bhai
dialogues.text: Honestly, I don't hate him at all. When he was young, he was passionate and talkative. He knew a great deal about poetry and singing, and I found that quite enviable.

dialogues.speaker: Bhai
dialogues.text: But now, his attitude is really driving me nuts. He could've done so much better than this!

dialogues.speaker: Bhai
dialogues.text: Shouldn't we who are alive cherish what we have and live in the present instead of trapping ourselves in the past?

dialogues.speaker: Bhai
dialogues.text: Old memories should nourish new life instead of becoming shackles that keep you in an endless loop of pain.

dialogues.speaker: Bhai
dialogues.text: I mean, the Dendro Archon may have lost much of her power, but that lost power became the nutrients required to save the world!

dialogues.speaker: Bhai
dialogues.text: That crusty old fellow has lived in Sumeru for so long, and yet, he doesn't understand this. He hasn't learned a thing from her at all!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Cherish what I have...

dialogues.speaker: Bhai
dialogues.text: When I was young, I used to travel around with the fleet, which taught me to cherish every drop of water and every flower.

dialogues.speaker: Bhai
dialogues.text: The surging waves, the soaring seagulls, or the swaying seaweed on the shores are all testaments to life.

dialogues.speaker: Bhai
dialogues.text: You'll understand that when you get to see as much as I have. Don't follow in that old fogey's footsteps!
